key_insight: PDI-Bench introduces a single, quantitative Perspective Distortion Index that detects geometric incoherence in generated video clips by measuring violations of perspective/projective consistency across frames, enabling automatic and interpretable diagnosis of 3D/motion failures.
problem_solved: Replaces subjective human or learned graders with an objective, diagnostic metric to reveal when generative video/world models produce physically implausible 3D structure or camera motion.
method: Extract geometric cues from each frame (line segments, vanishing points, sparse depth/correspondences) and estimate per-frame projective parameters.
Compute temporal consistency of perspective — a Perspective Distortion Index (PDI) that quantifies deviations from a coherent 3D projection across frames.
Benchmark generated clips against real-video baselines and provide per-clip/per-model diagnostics for geometric failure modes.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with an automated, interpretable evaluation tool to benchmark, debug, and improve generative video and implicit world models by focusing on physically meaningful geometric errors.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: clip → geometric cue extraction → camera/depth estimation → PDI calculation → score/report
Example frames with overlaid line segments and vanishing points showing consistent vs. inconsistent perspective
Bar chart comparing PDI scores across models/datasets to rank geometric fidelity
Temporal heatmap/timeline visualizing where in a clip perspective distortion spikes
paper_title: Quantitative Video World Model Evaluation for Geometric-Consistency
paper_authors: Jiaxin Wu, Yihao Pi, Yinling Zhang, Yuheng Li, Xueyan Zou
